mainTopic: Releasing and marrying a יבמה: מאמר, ביאה without מאמר and rabbinic lashes, the יבם's כתובה, and a limited גט for a יבמה
overview: The amud opens by fixing a mismatch in the משנה. Its heading says 'גט after גט,' but its example is מאמר and then a גט. רב יהודה explains that the example starts a new question, and after מאמר and a גט, חליצה is still needed. Next, the גמרא asks whether the משנה's line 'מאמר then ביאה is according to its מצוה' supports רב הונא. It concludes that ביאה without מאמר still acquires the יבמה, though the יבם gets rabbinic מכת מרדות for immodesty. This leads to a list of people רב flogged for improper conduct, and נהרדעא say he flogged only for betrothal through ביאה. A ברייתא then explains how מאמר is done, and אביי shows that its 'document' means the יבם's כתובה, which is paid from the first husband's property or else from the יבם. אביי then asks רבה about a limited גט to a יבמה, and רבה rules it disqualifies her, because it has ריח הגט and forbids a woman to a כהן. The amud ends with רמי בר חמא's rule about a גט written for an ארוסה, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The case described does not match the heading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is puzzled: the משנה's heading speaks of 'גט after גט,' but the example it gives is מאמר followed by גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this really a case of a גט after a גט?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a mismatch in the משנה. It promised to explain 'a גט after a גט,' but the example it gives is מאמר followed by a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The heading and the example don't line up. That makes the משנה look as though it is explaining the wrong case. The גמרא wants to know how the example fits the heading.

keyTerms.meaning: Rabbinic 'levirate betrothal,' where the יבם gives the יבמה money or a document to start the bond

phrases.english: Is this a case of a bill of divorce after a bill of divorce?
phrases.notes: The case in the משנה is really מאמר and then a גט, so it doesn't seem to match the heading.

steps.kashyaTarget: The way the משנה's example lines up with its heading
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The heading promises 'גט after גט,' but the example is 'מאמר then גט,' so they don't match.

steps.title: רב יהודה: the earlier cases were already explained, and this is a new topic
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that 'גט after גט' and 'מאמר after מאמר' were already covered. The example belongs to a new question: how one יבם and one יבמה are released.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: this is what the משנה means. 'A גט after a גט' and 'a מאמר after a מאמר' are as we already explained. But with one יבם and one יבמה, how are they released? If he did מאמר with his יבמה and gave her a גט, she still needs חליצה from him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה rereads the משנה so the example no longer belongs under the old heading. It starts a new topic about one יבם and one יבמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mismatch disappears because the 'כיצד' (how so?) now starts a fresh question, not the earlier heading. The new rule: after מאמר and a גט, the bond from יבום is still there, so חליצה is still needed.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means (a reread of the text)
Their release (permission to be free of the bond)
The ceremony that frees a יבמה from the יבם

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a גט alone does not fully end the bond of יבום after מאמר. חליצה is still required.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: This is what he is saying:

phrases.aramaic: גֵּט אַחַר הַגֵּט, וּמַאֲמָר אַחַר מַאֲמָר — כְּדַאֲמַרַן,
phrases.english: A bill of divorce after the bill of divorce, and levirate betrothal after levirate betrothal, are as we said,

phrases.aramaic: יָבָם אֶחָד וִיבָמָה אַחַת כֵּיצַד הַתָּרָתָן?
phrases.english: But one yavam and one yevama, how is their release done?

phrases.aramaic: עָשָׂה מַאֲמָר בִּיבִמְתּוֹ וְנָתַן לָהּ גֵּט —
phrases.english: If he performed levirate betrothal with his yevama and gave her a bill of divorce,
she requires ḥalitza from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the mismatch raised in step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the משנה: the example starts a new topic
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The example was meant to explain the heading 'גט after גט.'
steps.terutzMaskana: The heading cases were already explained. The example teaches how one יבם and one יבמה are released: after מאמר and גט, חליצה is still needed.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: מאמר then ביאה is according to its מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line from the משנה it is about to discuss.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did מאמר and then had relations with her, this is according to its מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה. This sets up the next move, where it will ask what the line proves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The line says that doing מאמר first and then ביאה is the proper way to do the מצוה. The open question is whether it means this is the ONLY proper way.

keyTerms.meaning: According to its מצוה (the proper way)

phrases.aramaic: עָשָׂה מַאֲמָר וּבָעַל — הֲרֵי זוֹ כְּמִצְוָתָהּ.
phrases.english: If he performed levirate betrothal and engaged in intercourse, this is in accordance with its מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: עָשָׂה מַאֲמָר וּבָעַל הֲרֵי זוֹ כְּמִצְוָתָהּ
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מאמר followed by ביאה is the proper way to do the מצוה of יבום.

steps.title: Does the משנה support רב הונא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה backs רב הונא, who says the ideal מצוה is קידושין first and then ביאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this supports רב הונא? For רב הונא said: the מצוה of a יבמה is that he first betroths her and afterward has relations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests this משנה is a proof for רב הונא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה calls 'מאמר then ביאה' the proper way, that suggests מאמר is a needed part of the ideal מצוה. That is exactly what רב הונא says.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say it supports him?

phrases.english: Let us say that this supports Rav Huna,
as Rav Huna said:

phrases.aramaic: מִצְוַת יְבָמָה — מְקַדֵּשׁ וְאַחַר כָּךְ בּוֹעֵל.
phrases.english: The מצוה of a yevama is that he betroths and afterward engages in intercourse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from the משנה line quoted in step 3
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's rule that the ideal מצוה is מאמר first and then ביאה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: 'עשה מאמר ובעל הרי זו כמצותה'

steps.title: Reread: this TOO is according to its מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed away. The משנה may only mean that מאמר then ביאה is ALSO a proper way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: this too is according to its מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by reading the משנה as 'this ALSO is fine,' not 'this is the only proper way.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the word 'also,' the משנה no longer says מאמר is required for the ideal מצוה. So it gives no support to רב הונא.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying רב הונא is wrong. It is only saying this משנה doesn't prove him right.

phrases.english: Say: This too is in accordance with its מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in step 4
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the משנה. רב הונא's view itself is left standing.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the משנה describes the only proper way. It can be read as one acceptable way.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה only means 'this too is fine,' why does it need to say so?
steps.simpleTranslation: That's obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה would bother teaching something so obvious, once it is read as 'this too is fine.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding מאמר before ביאה should not ruin anything. So telling us it is still acceptable seems unnecessary.

phrases.english: Isn't this obvious?

steps.kashyaTarget: The reading 'אף זה כמצותה' from step 5
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If מאמר first is just one acceptable way, there seems to be no need to say it.

steps.title: You might think מאמר removes the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה was needed. Since מאמר replaces the bond of יבום with a bond of ordinary marriage, one might think the later ביאה is no longer a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: since the master said that one who does מאמר with his יבמה makes the bond of יבום fly away from himself, and a bond of אירוסין and נישואין takes hold of him, then he is no longer doing a מצוה. So the משנה teaches us that he is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה's teaching is not obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There was an earlier teaching that מאמר turns the bond of יבום into a bond of regular marriage. From that, you might think the ביאה afterward is just regular marriage and not the מצוה of יבום. The משנה tells us it is still a מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: It might have entered your mind to say
The bond of יבום between the יבם and the יבמה

phrases.english: It might enter your mind to say:
since the Master said:
One who performs levirate betrothal with his yevama
causes the levirate bond to fly away from him,
and a bond of betrothal and marriage takes effect on him,
you might say he is not performing a מצוה,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'פשיטא' challenge of step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a reasonable mistaken idea (הוה אמינא) that the משנה had to correct
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since מאמר replaces the bond of יבום with a bond of marriage, the ביאה afterward might not count as a מצוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: מאמר followed by ביאה is still a proper fulfillment of the מצוה of יבום.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה does not prove that מאמר is required. It teaches that doing מאמר first does not cancel the מצוה.

steps.title: רב הונא's full statement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רב הונא's statement in full: the ideal is קידושין and then ביאה, and if he had ביאה and then did מאמר, he acquired her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the statement itself. רב הונא said: the מצוה of יבום is that he first betroths and afterward has relations. And if he had relations and then did מאמר, he has acquired her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to discuss רב הונא's statement on its own, quoting it in full.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The statement has two parts: the ideal order, and a second clause about what happens if the order is different. The second clause is about to be examined.

keyTerms.meaning: He acquired her (she is his wife)

phrases.english: Regarding the matter itself, Rav Huna said:

phrases.aramaic: מִצְוַת יְבָמִין — מְקַדֵּשׁ וְאַחַר כָּךְ בּוֹעֵל,
phrases.english: The מצוה of levirate marriage is that he betroths and afterward engages in intercourse,
and if he engaged in intercourse and performed levirate betrothal, he has acquired her.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ideal order: מאמר, then ביאה. If he had ביאה and then did מאמר, he acquired her.

steps.title: Obvious: ביאה already acquired her
steps.stepSummary: The second clause seems pointless, because ביאה alone already acquires the יבמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he had relations and then did מאמר, that's obvious, since he already acquired her through ביאה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second clause of רב הונא's statement as obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once ביאה happens, she is already acquired. A מאמר afterward adds nothing, so there is no reason to say 'he acquired her.'

keyTerms.meaning: Marital relations, the act that completes יבום

phrases.english: If he engaged in intercourse and performed levirate betrothal, it is obvious,
as he has already acquired her through intercourse!

steps.kashyaTarget: The second clause of רב הונא's statement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ביאה acquires her on its own, so a later מאמר is meaningless and the clause teaches nothing.

steps.title: Corrected wording: ביאה without מאמר acquires
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the wording: if he had ביאה without any מאמר, he still acquired her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: if he had relations without מאמר, he has acquired her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes the wording of רב הונא's second clause so that it teaches something real.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא meant that skipping מאמר does not stop the acquisition. Doing מאמר first is the ideal, but it is not required for the יבום to take effect.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב הונא, the ideal is מאמר and then ביאה. But ביאה alone, without מאמר, fully acquires the יבמה.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
If he engaged in intercourse without levirate betrothal, he has acquired her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא אִם בָּעַל בְּלֹא מַאֲמָר קָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9 by fixing the wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The clause read 'ביאה and then מאמר,' which seemed to teach nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The clause means ביאה without מאמר still acquires her.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: מאמר before ביאה is the ideal, but ביאה alone completes the acquisition.

steps.title: But a ברייתא says he gets lashes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that ביאה without מאמר is fine, because a ברייתא teaches that such a יבם is flogged.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא that he is flogged?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question on what it just said. If ביאה without מאמר works, why does a ברייתא say the יבם gets lashes?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 said the ביאה without מאמר still acquires the יבמה. Lashes usually mean someone did something forbidden. So the ברייתא seems to say this way of acting is wrong, which seems to clash with treating it as acceptable.

keyTerms.meaning: He is flogged; he gets lashes.
A teaching from the time of the משנה that was not included in the משנה.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught that he is flogged?!
phrases.notes: "He" is the יבם who had ביאה without doing מאמר first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of Step 10 that ביאה without מאמר is effective and acceptable.
steps.kashyaTarget: The statement that a יבם who had ביאה without מאמר acquired the יבמה (Step 10).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא gives lashes for this act, and lashes suggest the act is forbidden. That seems to clash with treating it as an acceptable way to acquire her.

steps.title: Only rabbinic lashes for improper behavior
steps.stepSummary: The lashes are מכת מרדות from the חכמים for acting in an immodest way. They do not mean the ביאה failed to work.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those are lashes for rebelliousness, from the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The lashes in the ברייתא are only a rabbinic punishment for behaving improperly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer separates two questions: does the act work, and was it done properly? The ביאה still acquires the יבמה, but the חכמים punish him because skipping מאמר and going straight to ביאה is not modest behavior.

keyTerms.meaning: Lashes for rebelliousness. A punishment the חכמים give for going against their rules or for improper conduct.
From the חכמים (a rabbinic law), not from the תורה.

steps.confusionAlert: The lashes do not mean the ביאה is invalid. He still acquired her; he is only punished for the improper way he did it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common idea across the גמרא: an act can fully work legally and still be punished by the חכמים because of the manner in which it was done.

phrases.english: Lashes for rebelliousness, from the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the source: the lashes in the ברייתא are rabbinic, not because the act was invalid or forbidden by the תורה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Lashes would mean the ביאה without מאמר is forbidden, so treating it as acceptable would be wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ביאה works. The lashes are only מכת מרדות for immodest conduct.

steps.title: רב's list of people he flogged
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the idea of rabbinic lashes for improper conduct by listing cases where רב gave lashes, even though most of these acts work legally.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב would flog a man who marries a woman through ביאה, a man who marries in the marketplace, and a man who marries without a prior match. He would also flog a man who cancels a גט and a man who makes a declaration beforehand that undercuts a גט. He would flog someone who disrespects a messenger of the חכמים. And he would flog someone who stays under a שמתא from the חכמים for thirty days without coming to the בית דין to ask that it be lifted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer by showing that רב really did give rabbinic lashes. Most items on the list are legally effective acts done in an improper way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first three cases are about how a man marries: they work, but they are crude or immodest, just like our יבם. The next two are ways of cancelling or undercutting a גט that work but can mislead the wife. The last two are about disrespecting the authority of the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: A match or agreement arranged before the marriage.
A declaration made beforehand that something he will do is not of his own free will.
A messenger of the חכמים (for example, from the בית דין).
A ban (נידוי) placed on someone by the חכמים.

steps.whatToRemember: A יבם who has ביאה without מאמר still acquires the יבמה, but he gets rabbinic lashes for immodest conduct. רב gave similar lashes for many acts that work legally but are done improperly.

phrases.english: For רב would flog one who betroths through intercourse,
and one who betroths in the marketplace,
and one who betroths without a prior match arrangement.
And one who cancels a bill of divorce,
phrases.notes: He means a man who sent a גט and then cancels it before it reaches his wife.

phrases.english: and one who makes a declaration against a bill of divorce.
phrases.notes: He tells witnesses ahead of time that he is giving the גט against his will, which can make it invalid.

phrases.english: one who acts disrespectfully toward a messenger of the Rabbis,
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added by the corrected wording.

phrases.english: and one who stays with a ban of the Rabbis on him
for thirty days,
and does not come to the court
and ask about his ban.
phrases.notes: He means asking the בית דין to lift the ban.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of Step 12 by showing רב gave rabbinic lashes for acts that work legally but are done improperly.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the lashes for ביאה without מאמר are rabbinic מכת מרדות for improper conduct.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's practice of flogging people for improper behavior, such as marrying through ביאה, in the marketplace, or without a prior match, along with other cases.

steps.title: The last case on the list: a son-in-law living with his in-laws
steps.stepSummary: The list of people רב flogged ends with a son-in-law who lives in his father-in-law's house.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב also flogged a son-in-law who lives in his father-in-law's house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the list from the last step of people רב flogged for improper conduct. The last item is a son-in-law who lives in his in-laws' home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Living there is not forbidden by the תורה, so these lashes are clearly rabbinic. That fits the claim of step 13 that רב gave lashes for behavior that is improper even when it is not an actual sin.

phrases.english: And for a son-in-law who lives
phrases.notes: This continues the list of people רב flogged. The word 'flogged' is carried over from the earlier items.

phrases.english: in his father-in-law's house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final item of the list of רב's lashes begun in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: That חכמים give lashes for improper behavior that is not a Torah sin
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's practice of flogging a son-in-law who lives in his in-laws' house

steps.title: What about a son-in-law who only passes by?
steps.stepSummary: The wording suggests that only living there gets lashes, but רב ששת flogged a man who just passed his in-laws' door.
steps.simpleTranslation: Only one who lives there is flogged, but one who passes by is not? But a certain man passed by the doorway of his father-in-law's house, and רב ששת flogged him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the word 'lives' as excluding someone who only passes by. Then it challenges that reading with a story about רב ששת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If lashes are only for living there, why did רב ששת flog a man who just walked past the door? The story seems to show that even passing by gets lashes.

phrases.english: One who lives there — yes,
but one who just passes by — no?
But there was a certain man who passed
by the doorway of his father-in-law's house,
and רב ששת flogged him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference from the word 'lives' in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication that only a son-in-law who lives there is flogged
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב ששת flogged a man who only passed by, so passing by also seems to deserve lashes.

steps.title: That man was under suspicion
steps.stepSummary: The man רב ששת flogged was suspected with his mother-in-law, so his case was special.
steps.simpleTranslation: That man was suspected of an improper relationship with his mother-in-law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the story was an unusual case. That man had a bad reputation with his mother-in-law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally just passing by does not get lashes. Because this man was already suspected, even passing her door supported the rumors, so רב ששת flogged him. The general rule still applies only to one who lives there.

phrases.english: That man was suspected
in connection with his mother-in-law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב ששת's story shows that anyone who passes by is flogged.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a suspected man is flogged for passing by. Others are flogged only for living there.

steps.title: נהרדעא's view: רב only flogged for betrothal through ביאה without a match agreement
steps.stepSummary: The scholars of נהרדעא say רב gave lashes in none of these cases except for betrothal through ביאה with no earlier match agreement.
steps.simpleTranslation: The people of נהרדעא say: In all of these cases רב did not flog, except for one who betroths through ביאה without a match agreement beforehand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another version of רב's practice from the scholars of נהרדעא. They say the long list is not right, and רב flogged in only one case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By this view, רב flogged only for betrothal through ביאה done without first arranging the match. That is the most immodest way to marry. The other items on the list did not get lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: the scholars of the city נהרדעא

phrases.english: The people of נהרדעא say:
In all of these cases רב would not flog,
except one who betroths through relations
and without a match agreement beforehand.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְהַרְדָּעֵי אָמְרִי: בְּכוּלְּהוּ לָא מְנַגֵּיד רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a narrower account of the list of רב's lashes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב flogged only one who betrothed through ביאה without an earlier match agreement.

steps.title: Some say: even with a match agreement
steps.stepSummary: Another version says רב flogged for betrothal through ביאה even when a match agreement came first, because of the immodesty.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: even with a match agreement too, because of the immodesty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the נהרדעא view. It says the lashes were given for betrothal through ביאה in every case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first version blames the missing match agreement. This version says betrothal through ביאה is immodest in itself, so an earlier agreement does not help. That fits step 12, where a יבם doing ביאה without מאמר is flogged for immodesty.

phrases.english: And some say:
even with a match agreement too, he would flog
because of the immodesty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second version of the נהרדעא view in step 17, which makes the lashes broader.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב flogged for any betrothal through ביאה, even with a match agreement, because it is immodest.
steps.whatToRemember: Every version agrees that betrothal through ביאה can bring rabbinic lashes for immodesty. The ביאה still works legally.

steps.title: How is מאמר done? With money
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a יבם does מאמר by giving the יבמה money or something worth money.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: How is מאמר done? He gives her money or something worth money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ברייתא. It explains how a יבם does מאמר, the rabbinic betrothal of a יבמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מאמר works like a regular betrothal. The יבם gives the יבמה money or an item worth money to betroth her.

keyTerms.meaning: rabbinic betrothal of a יבמה by the יבם

phrases.english: The רבנן taught:
How is מאמר done?

phrases.aramaic: נָתַן לָהּ כֶּסֶף אוֹ שָׁוֶה כֶּסֶף.
phrases.english: He gives her money or something worth money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: how מאמר is done.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מאמר is done by giving money or something worth money.

steps.title: The ברייתא asks: and how with a document?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא goes on to ask how it is done with a document.
steps.simpleTranslation: And with a document, how is it done?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a second question about using a document. This sets up the גמרא's surprise in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first the question seems to ask how to do מאמר with a betrothal document. The next step explains why that reading is a problem.

phrases.english: And with a document, how is it done?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with a second question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How a document is used here

steps.title: Why ask? The rules of a betrothal document are already known
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised by the question, since we already learned how betrothal with a document works.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a document, how?! As we said: he writes to her on paper or a piece of pottery, even if it is not worth a פרוטה, 'You are betrothed to me'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the ברייתא's question in surprise. It reminds us that we already know how betrothal with a document works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A betrothal document works through its words, not its value, so writing 'you are betrothed to me' on anything is enough. Since we already know this, the ברייתא's question seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: worth a פרוטה, the smallest coin value

steps.confusionAlert: The same Hebrew words 'בשטר כיצד' appear twice. The first time they are the ברייתא's question. The second time they are the גמרא asking in surprise why the question was needed.

phrases.english: With a document, how?!
phrases.notes: The גמרא repeats the question in surprise, as if to say: why would you even ask?

phrases.english: It is as we said:

phrases.aramaic: כָּתַב לָהּ עַל הַנְּיָיר אוֹ עַל הַחֶרֶס,
phrases.english: he writes to her on paper or on a piece of pottery,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה:
phrases.english: even if it is not worth a פרוטה:
'You are hereby betrothed to me'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the ברייתא's question in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's question 'and with a document, how?'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rules of a betrothal document are already known, so there is nothing new to ask.

steps.title: אביי: it means the יבם's כתובה document
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the ברייתא is asking how to write the כתובה for a יבמה, not a betrothal document.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said, this is what it means: How is the document of a כתובה for יבמין written?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by reading the ברייתא's question in a new way. 'Document' means the כתובה the יבם writes for her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once 'document' means the כתובה, the question is no longer about betrothal, which we already know. It asks something new: what does the יבם's כתובה say?

keyTerms.meaning: the כתובה written for a יבמה by the יבם

phrases.english: אביי said, this is what it means:
How is the document of a כתובה for יבמין written?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21 by reading the question differently.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question was about a betrothal document, which we already know.
steps.terutzMaskana: The question is about the wording of the יבם's כתובה.

steps.title: The wording of the יבם's כתובה
steps.stepSummary: The יבם writes that he accepts his יבמה and will support her, while her כתובה stays on her first husband's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: He writes to her: 'I, so-and-so son of so-and-so, have accepted my יבמה so-and-so upon myself, to feed and support her properly, on condition that her כתובה is on the property of her first husband.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question by giving the actual words of the יבם's כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The יבם promises to support her like a husband. But her כתובה money still comes from her first husband's property, not from the יבם's own.

keyTerms.meaning: the property of her first husband

phrases.english: He writes to her:
'I, so-and-so son of so-and-so,
have accepted so-and-so, my יבמה, upon myself,
to feed and support her properly,
on condition that her כתובה is
on the property of her first husband.'

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּתַב לַהּ: אֲנָא פְּלוֹנִי בַּר פְּלוֹנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question as אביי explained it.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The wording of the כתובה: he accepts and supports her, and her כתובה is on the first husband's property.

steps.title: If the first husband left nothing, the יבם pays
steps.stepSummary: If the first husband has no property, the רבנן made the כתובה come from the יבם, so he will not divorce her easily.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if she has nothing from the first husband, the רבנן arranged for her to collect from the second, so that it will not be easy in his eyes to divorce her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a rabbinic rule for when the first husband left no property. Then the יבם's own property backs the כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason is the same as for every כתובה. If divorce costs him nothing, he might send her away over something small. Making the יבם liable protects her.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the purpose of a כתובה, to protect the wife from an easy divorce, applies to a יבמה too.
steps.whatToRemember: A יבמה's כתובה normally comes from her first husband's property. If he left nothing, the רבנן made the יבם pay, so she still has protection.

phrases.english: And if she has nothing from the first husband —
the רבנן arranged for her to collect from the second,
phrases.notes: 'The second' is the יבם, her second husband.

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא תְּהֵא קַלָּה בְּעֵינָיו לְהוֹצִיאָהּ.
phrases.english: so that it will not be easy in his eyes to divorce her.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי לֵית לַהּ מֵרִאשׁוֹן — תַּקִּינוּ לַהּ רַבָּנַן מִשֵּׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a rabbinic rule for a case the כתובה wording does not cover.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the first husband left no property, the יבמה's כתובה is collected from the יבם, so he will not divorce her lightly.

steps.title: אביי asks about a limited divorce given to a יבמה
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רבה what happens if a יבם gives his יבמה a גט that says she is divorced from him but not permitted to any other man.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי asked רבה: If a יבם gave his יבמה a גט and said, 'You are divorced from me, but you are not permitted to any man,' what is the law? Since a יבמה's גט is only rabbinic, maybe it follows the rules of a regular גט: whatever works for an אשת איש works for a יבמה, and whatever does not work for an אשת איש does not work for a יבמה. Or maybe we worry that people will confuse it with a real גט.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks a new question about a גט with a strange limit on it, given by a יבם to his יבמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a regular married woman, a גט that does not let her marry others is not a real גט at all. The question is whether the rabbinic גט of a יבמה works the same way, so it would do nothing, or whether חכמים gave it force anyway because people might mix it up with a normal גט.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked of him, a real question looking for an answer
The divorce document a יבם gives his יבמה
To confuse or mix up one thing with another

phrases.english: Abaye asked of Rabba:
If he gave her a bill of divorce and said:
phrases.notes: "He" is the יבם, and "her" is his יבמה.

phrases.english: "You are hereby divorced from me,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַתְּ מוּתֶּרֶת לְכׇל אָדָם״. מַהוּ?
phrases.english: but you are not permitted to any man" — what is the law?
Is a yevama's bill of divorce rabbinic,

phrases.aramaic: גֵּט דְּמַהֲנֵי בְּאֵשֶׁת אִישׁ — מַהֲנֵי בִּיבָמָה,
phrases.english: so a get that works for a married woman works for a yevama,

phrases.aramaic: גֵּט דְּלָא מַהֲנֵי בְּאֵשֶׁת אִישׁ — לָא מַהֲנֵי בִּיבָמָה,
phrases.english: and a get that does not work for a married woman does not work for a yevama,
or perhaps people will come to confuse it with a real get?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about a גט given to a יבמה, moving on from the כתובה of the יבמה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a גט that divorces the יבמה from the יבם but does not permit her to others have any effect?

steps.title: רבה answers that we worry about confusion
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that we are concerned people will confuse this גט with a regular גט, so it does have an effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We are concerned that perhaps people will come to confuse it with a real גט.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה picks the second side of אביי's question: the limited גט does have an effect on the יבמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a regular married woman, this kind of גט does not free her to remarry. Still, for a יבמה the חכמים give it force, because people seeing it might think it was a normal גט from a יבם. So she becomes disqualified from the יבם.

keyTerms.meaning: We are concerned, we take the worry seriously

phrases.english: He said to him: We are concerned
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording; the speaker is רבה.

phrases.english: that perhaps people will come to confuse it with a real get.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question from step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The limited גט does affect the יבמה, because people might confuse it with a full גט.

steps.title: רבה בר חנן asks about a blank piece of paper
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר חנן challenges רבה: if we worry so much about confusion, then even a blank piece of paper should disqualify her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר חנן objected: But if so, if he gives her a mere piece of paper, would it also disqualify her?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר חנן attacks רבה's answer by stretching it to an extreme case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the only reason is that people might confuse things, then a יבם handing her any paper at all could cause confusion. Surely a blank paper does nothing, so the reason seems too broad.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so, then by your logic

phrases.english: Rabba bar Hanan strongly objected:
But if so,
if he gives her a mere piece of paper,
would it also disqualify her?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבָּה בַּר חָנָן: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's answer in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's reason that we worry people will confuse the limited גט with a real one.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reduction to an absurd result: the same worry would apply to a blank paper, yet a blank paper obviously does nothing.

steps.title: A blank paper does nothing, but this גט disqualifies for כהונה
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that a blank paper has no effect even on a married woman, while this limited גט already disqualifies a woman from marrying a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There, a blank paper does not disqualify her from כהונה. Here, this גט does disqualify her from כהונה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה defends his answer by showing a real difference between a blank paper and the limited גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blank paper does nothing to anyone, so there is no reason to give it force. The limited גט already has some legal power, since even for a married woman it forbids her to a כהן. Because it has that real effect, חכמים also let it disqualify the יבמה.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָתָם לָא פָּסֵיל בִּכְהוּנָּה,
phrases.english: He said to him: There, it does not disqualify her from the priesthood;
here, it does disqualify her from the priesthood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָתָם לָא פָּסֵיל בִּכְהוּנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The worry about confusion would apply to any paper the יבם gives.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a document that already has some legal effect, like forbidding her to a כהן, is given force for a יבמה.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows that a limited גט forbids a woman to a כהן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the פסוק that even a woman divorced only from her husband, without being permitted to others, is forbidden to a כהן. This is called ריח הגט.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: 'And a woman divorced from her husband they shall not take.' Even if she was only divorced from her husband, 'they shall not take' her. This is the ריח הגט that disqualifies from כהונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove what רבה just said, that a limited גט forbids a woman to a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says "divorced from her husband," which hints that being divorced from him alone is enough. So a גט that does not free her to others still has a small trace of divorce, the ריח הגט, which is enough to forbid her to a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: They shall not take, the כהנים may not marry her
The 'scent' of a get, a weak trace of divorce

steps.whatToRemember: A limited גט ('divorced from me but not permitted to others') is not a full divorce, but it has ריח הגט: it forbids a woman to a כהן. Because it has that much power, it also disqualifies a יבמה.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of ריח הגט shows that a document can have partial legal effect even when it fails as a full divorce.

phrases.english: As it is taught:
"And a woman divorced from her husband they shall not take";
even if she was divorced only from her husband,
phrases.notes: He means the גט freed her only from him, not to marry other men.

phrases.english: "they shall not take" her.
And this is the "scent" of a get
that disqualifies her from the priesthood.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: וְאִשָּׁה גְּרוּשָׁה מֵאִישָׁהּ לֹא יִקָּחוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the claim in step 28.
steps.raayaObject: That a limited גט disqualifies a woman from marrying a כהן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading ויקרא 21:7, "divorced from her husband".

steps.title: רמי בר חמא: a גט may be written for an ארוסה to use after נישואין
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא quotes a rule: if a man tells a scribe to write a גט for his ארוסה so he can divorce her after marrying her, the גט is valid, because he already has the power to divorce her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said: They said that if a man told a scribe, 'Write a גט for my betrothed; when I marry her, I will divorce her,' it is a valid גט, because it is already in his power to divorce her.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא brings a new rule about writing a גט ahead of time. This sets up the next discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a גט must be written when the man is able to divorce the woman. Here the ארוסה is already tied to him by קידושין, so he can divorce her right now. That is why a גט written during the אירוסין may be used even after the נישואין.

keyTerms.meaning: They have said, quoting an accepted rule
My betrothed, a woman with קידושין but not yet נישואין
It is in his power to divorce her

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא: הֲרֵי אָמְרוּ,
phrases.english: Rami bar Hama said: They have said,
if one said to a scribe:
"Write a bill of divorce for my betrothed,
so that when I marry her, I will divorce her" —
it is a valid bill of divorce,
because it is in his power to divorce her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא: הֲרֵי אָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about writing a גט ahead of time, which the גמרא will go on to discuss.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט written for an ארוסה, to be given after the נישואין, is valid because the man already has the power to divorce her.
